extracted.intended_audience: academics and researchers who act as journal peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting constructive, usable peer reviews of academic manuscripts for journal editors and authors, covering structure, tone, level of detail, and recommendation justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a (very) brief summary of the paper, then an editorial overview, then detailed comments organized by severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments so editors can quickly grasp the main evaluation (summary + high-level editorial view) and then see clearly separated major versus minor issues in the detailed section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: "A good review does not just criticise but also highlights what the authors have done well."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out strengths as well as weaknesses so authors understand what to preserve and editors see the full picture of the manuscript's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be clear, constructive, consistent, and professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language that helps authors improve the work; avoid sarcasm, hostility, or vague negativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justified recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final verdict should align with detailed comments so editors can justify decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your overall recommendation (accept/revise/reject) follows logically from the specific, evidenced criticisms and suggestions you provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unprofessional language (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid insulting or derogatory terms which undermine credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use personal attacks or demeaning phrases; unprofessional language damages both the reviewer's influence and the review's usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor organization (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An unstructured stream of consciousness" that fails to distinguish major from minor issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not deliver disorganized lists of comments; group and prioritize problems so editors and authors can act efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient detail (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that are too brief for editors to understand your reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough evidence and explanation for each criticism so editors can evaluate its severity and authors can respond or revise appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive demands (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring unnecessary revisions beyond what's needed for publishability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between essential changes required for publication and optional improvements; avoid requesting work that is disproportionate to the manuscript's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreasonable expectations (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommending changes authors cannot feasibly implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider practical constraints (scope, time, data availability) when suggesting revisions; avoid asking for entirely new studies or unattainable analyses as a condition for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key rule — tone you would be happy to receive
rubrics_metrics.description: Write reviews "in a tone you would be happy to receive," keeping both editors and authors as your audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt empathetic, professional phrasing and imagine how your words will be interpreted by the authors; this helps ensure usefulness and civility.
